Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Third Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are David Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; Jennifer Hayes, Chief Operating Officer; Mark Esposito, Chief Claims Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to David Reynolds.

David Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for the third quarter. We delivered strong results, driven by robust share repurchase activity, the effectiveness of our reinsurance program, strategic asset allocation across fixed income, equities, and alternatives, favorable loss ratio trends amid managed claims frequency and severity, solid new business production volumes, clear combined ratio guidance for the coming periods, enhanced investment income yields, and improving expense ratio trends through commission efficiencies and operating cost controls. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

Michael Chen, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, David. Good morning, everyone. As David mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $850 million, or $2.45 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included strong underwriting margins, resilient investment returns, disciplined expense management, effective reinsurance recoveries, and opportunistic share repurchases. Our combined ratio was 92.5%. Investment income for the quarter was $1.4 billion. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with RBC ratio at 520%. Our expense ratio also improved to 28.5%.

Good afternoon, everyone—or good morning, depending on your time zone. Before we move deeper into the details and open the line for Q&A, I'd like to provide some color on our share repurchase activity during the quarter, which remains a cornerstone of our capital allocation framework here at Apex Insurance Group. As you know, we prioritize returning excess capital to shareholders in a disciplined manner, balancing repurchases against organic growth opportunities, M&A, and strategic bolt-ons in our Property & Casualty, Life & Health, and Reinsurance segments.

In the third quarter, we executed $650 million in share repurchases, bringing our year-to-date total to $2.1 billion. This represents approximately 65% utilization of our $3.2 billion program, which we announced in February following our successful $1.5 billion senior notes issuance at a blended 4.75% yield—allowing us to lock in favorable long-term funding amid the Fed's rate pause. On a trailing twelve-month basis, we've now retired over 28 million shares, or roughly 4.2% of our float, at an average price of $148.30 per share. This compares favorably to our current trading level around $162, underscoring the opportunistic nature of our approach.

Let me break down the trends and drivers. Q3 activity accelerated 25% sequentially from Q2's $520 million, fueled by robust free cash flow generation of $1.8 billion year-to-date—well ahead of our initial $1.4 billion guide. This was underpinned by our attritional combined ratio of 92.4% in the quarter, beating expectations by 110 basis points, thanks to premium rate adequacy in commercial lines up 8.2% ex-CAT and benign catastrophe losses at just $220 million pretax, primarily from secondary perils in the Southeast U.S. Investment income also contributed meaningfully, with our $145 billion portfolio yielding 4.6% annualized—boosted by our overweight in investment-grade corporates and RMBS, which benefited from the recent term premium expansion.

From a technical standpoint, we've leaned into algorithmic trading programs and 10b5-1 plans to execute efficiently, minimizing market impact. In Q3, 60% of repurchases were executed via dark pool and VWAP strategies during trading windows when our P/B ratio dipped below 1.4x—our key threshold calibrated against peers like Chubb and Travelers, who trade at 1.8x-2.0x. We avoided collars this quarter given the low volatility environment with VIX averaging 15, but we're monitoring for any re-entry if equity volatility spikes from election-related uncertainty.

Regionally, the capital deployment reflects our diversified footprint. North America, which accounts for 58% of our $42 billion in-force premiums, generated the lion's share of deployable capital—$1.2 billion YTD from P&C underwriting margins expanding to 14.5% ROE, driven by auto rate hikes mirroring Progressive's 10%+ comps and softening workers' comp loss trends. In EMEA, our Life & Health book contributed $450 million, with surplus capital from improved morbidity experience in UK group protection products, amid regulatory tailwinds from Solvency II optimizations. Asia-Pacific lagged slightly at $250 million, as we held back amid yen volatility impacting our Japan term life portfolio, but we expect acceleration in Q4 with premium growth resuming to 12% on the back of bancassurance partnerships similar to AIA's model.

Strategically, these repurchases are highly accretive: they've boosted diluted EPS by $2.15, or 8.7%, and enhanced book value per share by 3.2% to $112.40. This signals our confidence in our embedded value—our 15% compound organic growth target over the next five years, supported by 7-9% premium CAGR and a mid-teens ROE trajectory. We're not chasing yield at any cost; repurchases only when intrinsic value exceeds market price by 15%+, per our actuarial fair value models incorporating LDTI adjustments and IFRS 17 transition benefits.

Looking forward, we have $1.1 billion remaining under the current authorization, with no plans to announce an incremental program until our Q4 capital plan review. Deployment will remain flexible: if M&A opportunities emerge—like tuck-in deals in U.S. cyber or ESG-linked parametric insurance—we'll pivot, akin to how Markel has accreted through specialty acquisitions. Absent that, expect us to hit 85-90% utilization by year-end, assuming no material deterioration in our 93% full-year combined ratio guide or investment spreads compressing below 450 bps.

Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. As we review our Q3 results, I'd like to dive into one of the key pillars supporting our earnings stability and capital efficiency: the effectiveness of our reinsurance program. In an industry where volatility from natural catastrophes, cyber risks, and liability tail events can swing combined ratios by 20 points or more, our reinsurance strategy has been instrumental in delivering a net loss ratio of 58.2% this quarter—well below our peer average of 62.5%, per AM Best data—and shielding our RBC ratio at a robust 520%, up from 485% a year ago.

Let me start with the high-level metrics. For the nine months ended September 30th, our gross written premiums reached $18.7 billion, a 12% increase year-over-year, driven by strong commercial lines growth in property and casualty. We ceded $4.2 billion in premiums to reinsurers, equating to a 22.5% cession rate—strategically flat from last year despite the hardening market. This reflects our disciplined net retention of 77.5%, optimized across layers to balance risk transfer with cost efficiency. Our reinsurance expense ratio improved to 8.1% from 8.7% in the prior period, a 70 basis point gain, primarily from favorable quota share renewals and reduced friction costs in our collateralized programs.

Turning to performance, our program proved its mettle during the active 2023 North Atlantic hurricane season. Hurricane Idalia and the remnants of Lee generated $450 million in gross losses for us, predominantly in our Florida homeowners and Florida Citizens-like exposure book. Thanks to our multi-layered excess-of-loss towers—starting at $50 million attachment with Swiss Re on the first layer up to $1 billion ultimate, backed by Munich Re and Berkshire Hathaway on the upper decks—we recovered 96.8% of those losses, or $436 million, within 90 days. This compares favorably to the industry average recovery rate of 92% reported by S&P Global for similar events. Post-event, our net probable maximum loss for a 1-in-100-year U.S. Northeast hurricane event stands at just 4.2% of surplus, down from 5.1% pre-renewal, per our updated RMS v18.1 ProbCat modeling.

Regionally, the program's effectiveness shines through diversification. In the U.S., which accounts for 55% of our ceded premium, we've layered in catastrophe bonds via our $350 million issuance last December—listed on the Bermuda Stock Exchange—providing fully funded, multi-year protection against California wildfires and Gulf Coast windstorm at a blended cost of 4.2% versus traditional XoL at 6.1%. This alternative risk transfer layer, managed through our partnership with Nephila Capital now Markel CatCo, capped our net wildfire PML at $220 million for the 2023 Los Angeles Basin event sequence.

In Europe, representing 25% of cessions, our Solvency II-compliant program benefited from a 15% reduction in flood PML following the Storm Babet claims cycle, where we ceded 85% of €180 million gross losses through our proportional treaties with Hannover Re. We've also embedded cyber clash exclusions in line with market standards post the MOVEit breach fallout, limiting our net exposure to $75 million for a 1-in-200-year event.

Asia-Pacific, at 15% of cessions, saw outperformance amid Typhoon Mawar's impacts in Japan and the Philippines. Our facultative placements with SCOR and PartnerRe recovered 98% of $120 million gross losses, underscoring the value of our regional hubs in Singapore and Tokyo for tailored risk selection. Finally, our 5% emerging markets bucket—Latin America and MENA—utilizes parametric triggers via reinsurers like Validus, which paid out $28 million automatically after the Turkey-Syria earthquakes' aftershocks, minimizing disputes and leakage.

On technical initiatives, we've invested $25 million in our reinsurance optimization platform, powered by AI-driven cedent analytics from vendors like Verisk and Polychain. This has enabled dynamic layering: for instance, we've shifted 10% of our U.S. casualty book from traditional quota share 50% ceded to risk-attached XoL at lower attachments, reducing our tail risk VaR by 18% while maintaining a 12.5% RAROC target. We've also expanded collateralized reinsurance to 35% of our program up from 25% in 2022, posting $1.8 billion in LOC-backed trusts, which lowered acquisition costs amid the January 1st renewals where reinsurer pricing hardened 15-25% across P&C lines, per Guy Carpenter's barometer.

Strategically, this positions us for 2024 renewals exceptionally well. With $6.5 billion in limit expiring, we've secured 80% early at rates only 5% above expiring—half the market increase—thanks to our loss-free record and diversified portfolio. We're exploring sidecars for our casualty growth, targeting $500 million in third-party capital, akin to RenaissanceRe's success, to amplify underwriting leverage without diluting ROE. Looking ahead, we expect the reinsurance program to sustain our mid-90s combined ratio guidance, even in a 1-in-50-year cat year, while supporting 15% EPS growth through enhanced risk-adjusted returns.

Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. As we dive into our Q3 earnings, I'd like to provide a comprehensive update on our asset allocation strategy, which remains the cornerstone of our investment portfolio management here at Apex Insurance Group. Our $450 billion general account portfolio—comprising primarily life, annuity, and P&C liabilities—continues to deliver strong risk-adjusted returns while prioritizing capital preservation and liability matching. This quarter, our invested assets grew 4.2% year-over-year to $452.3 billion, driven by positive operating cash flows and prudent reinvestment of maturities.

Let me walk you through the high-level allocation as of September 30th, which reflects our disciplined asset-liability management framework. Fixed income remains our dominant holding at 72.5% of the portfolio, or $327.8 billion, down slightly from 74.1% at year-end 2023 as we tactically rotated into higher-yielding alternatives amid the Fed's rate normalization. Equities stand at 12.8%, or $57.9 billion, providing growth exposure with a focus on quality dividend payers. Alternatives have expanded to 11.2%, or $50.6 billion, up from 9.8% last year, underscoring our yield-enhancement strategy in a persistent low-to-moderate yield environment. The remainder, 3.5% or $15.8 billion, is in cash equivalents and short-duration instruments for liquidity and opportunistic deployments.

Starting with fixed income, our largest sleeve continues to anchor our portfolio with an average book yield of 4.65%, generating $4.1 billion in net investment income this quarter—up 8% YoY. We're heavily weighted toward investment-grade corporates 48% of fixed income, municipal bonds 15%, and U.S. Treasuries/agency MBS 22%, with the balance in RMBS and emerging market sovereigns for modest spread pickup.

Duration stands at 6.8 years, closely matching our intermediate-to-long-tail liabilities, particularly our fixed annuity blocks. We've maintained a conservative credit quality profile: 92% rated A or better, with just 3.2% in high-yield opportunistics. Regionally, North America dominates at 68% due to favorable spreads and liquidity, but we've increased our European exposure to 18%—targeting peripherals like Italian BTPs and covered bonds yielding 3.8-4.5%—as ECB policy divergence supports richer valuations. In Asia, our 14% allocation focuses on JGBs and SGD investment-grade credits, hedging currency risk via FX forwards to mitigate yen volatility.

A key technical initiative this quarter was our expanded use of interest rate swaps and Treasury futures in our derivatives overlay, notional $25 billion, which shortened effective duration by 0.4 years amid the 10-year Treasury yield climbing to 4.35%. This derisked our P&C book against potential rate spikes, while our LDI program with BlackRock's LifePath suite optimized matching for our $120 billion VA guaranteed living benefits.

Equities contributed 14% to total return YTD at 7.2%, outperforming the S&P 500's 6.8% on a beta-adjusted basis. Our $57.9 billion sleeve is 65% U.S. large-cap, emphasizing dividend aristocrats like Procter & Gamble and Johnson & Johnson yield ~3.0%, with 20% in global financials—banks like JPMorgan and HSBC for sector tailwinds from higher NIMs. International equities, at 15%, tilt toward Europe UK REITs and Swiss insurers for 4-5% dividend yields.

We've derisked via overlays: 40% covered call strategies through our partnership with PIMCO's equity income funds, generating an extra 120 bps of yield while capping upside in frothy markets. ROE targets remain above 12% for new positions, and our active managers—primarily Wellington and T. Rowe Price—have beaten benchmarks by 150 bps net of fees.

Alternatives have been our growth engine, now at 11.2% with a targeted book yield of 6.8%, contributing $850 million in income. Breakdown: private credit 4.1%, $18.5 billion via direct lending to middle-market sponsors like Ares and Owl Rock, yielding 8.5% net; core real estate 3.8%, $17.2 billion in multifamily and logistics via partnerships with Starwood and Blackstone, delivering 7.2% levered IRRs; and the rest in infrastructure 2.3% and hedge fund-of-funds 1.0% focused on credit long-short.

Strategically, we're navigating regulatory headwinds—such as NAIC's updated risk-based capital charges on illiquids—by capping alternatives at 15% and emphasizing RP replication portfolio modeling for liquidity stress tests. Regionally, U.S. privates dominate 55%, but Asia-Pacific exposure has doubled to 20% in renewables infrastructure e.g., solar farms in India via Brookfield, capitalizing on green bond subsidies and 9%+ yields. In Europe, we're selective in PE secondaries amid valuation resets post-Ukraine.

YTD, our portfolio returned 5.6% net of fees, with fixed income spreads tightening 15 bps but equities volatile from AI hype and election risks. Inflation at 2.6% has validated our TIPS allocation 2% of fixed income, hedging real yield erosion.

Key initiatives include AI-driven portfolio optimization via our in-house Quantum ALM platform, which simulates 10,000 scenarios daily for stochastic matching, and deeper ESG integration—20% of new fixed income flows into SFDR Article 8/9 bonds, aligning with EU Solvency II and our net-zero by 2050 pledge.

Looking ahead, we expect to maintain fixed income at 70-73%, gradually scaling alternatives to 13% by year-end through PA participating annuity runoff reinvestments. With the yield curve steepening, we'll opportunistically add 5-7 year corporates if spreads widen beyond 140 bps. Risks include prolonged high rates pressuring equity multiples and geopolitical flares in EM, but our 18% equity risk budget and $20 billion liquidity buffer position us resiliently.

This allocation not only supports our 12-14% ROE target but fortifies statutory capital at 520% RBC—well above peers.

Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. Moving now to our underwriting performance, I'll dive into the loss ratio trends and key drivers, which remain central to our disciplined execution in this dynamic environment. For the quarter, our consolidated combined ratio stood at 92.5%, reflecting a loss ratio of 62.8%—up 250 basis points year-over-year from 60.3% in Q3 last year, but down sequentially from 65.1% in Q2. Excluding catastrophe losses, our underlying loss ratio improved to 59.2%, a 40 basis point enhancement quarter-over-quarter, underscoring the efficacy of our pricing and underwriting actions amid persistent inflationary pressures.

Let me unpack the primary drivers: claims frequency and severity, with some color on cats and other externalities. Starting with frequency, we saw a modest 2.1% decline quarter-over-quarter across our personal lines portfolio, driven by favorable exposure trends. In auto, reported claims frequency per insured vehicle fell 3.5% YoY, benefiting from sustained lower miles driven—now at 92% of pre-pandemic levels per our telematics data from our Progressive-inspired Usage-Based Insurance program, which now covers 45% of our auto book. Homeowners frequency was flat, but commercial multi-peril saw a 1.8% uptick due to softening economic conditions pressuring small business exposures. Overall, frequency remains below our long-term plan of 1.5% annual growth, validating our shift toward higher-attachment deductibles and data-driven renewal selectivity.

On severity, this is where the story gets more challenged, contributing roughly 70% of the loss ratio expansion. Average claim costs rose 8.2% YoY, outpacing earned premium growth in several segments. In personal auto physical damage, severity surged 12.4% due to a perfect storm of OEM parts inflation—up 22% per CCC Intelligent Solutions data—labor rates climbing 15% amid technician shortages, and supply chain bottlenecks reminiscent of 2022. Our collision severity hit $4,800 per claim, a record high, exacerbated by EV repair complexities; we're now seeing 18% higher costs on Tesla and Rivian claims versus ICE vehicles. Bodily injury severity moderated to +6.1% after peaking at 11% in Q1, thanks to tort reform tailwinds in Florida and Texas, but litigation funding remains a headwind, with subrogation recovery rates dipping to 72% from 78% YoY.

Property lines tell a similar tale: homeowners severity increased 9.7% YoY to $28,400 per claim, fueled by reconstruction cost inflation—now 7.2% per CoreLogic indices—and rising reinsurance ceded costs. Cat losses totaled $245 million pre-tax this quarter, or 4.2 points to the loss ratio, primarily from Hurricane Milton analogs in the Southeast and California wildfire activity, which accounted for 60% of our $150 million in property cat hits. Comparatively, this is lighter than Travelers' $400 million cat book in Q3, reflecting our 25% reduction in coastal wind exposure since 2022 via zip code optimization.

Regionally, U.S. operations drove 85% of the mix, with a 64.2% loss ratio versus 58.9% in our international book. Europe benefited from milder weather and our partnership with AXA on cyber reinsurance, keeping severity flat, while Asia-Pacific saw +5% pressure from Typhoon Yagi-like events in our Japan property portfolio. Workers' comp severity eased 4.1% on lower medical trend—now 3.8% versus 5.2% industry per NCCI—bolstered by our AI-powered claims triage, which reduced cycle time by 22% and large loss notifications by 15%.

From a technical initiatives standpoint, we're leaning into tech to bend the curve. Our Genie AI platform, integrated with Verisk's weather analytics, flagged 12,000 high-risk policies for repricing, yielding a 4.5 point loss ratio benefit. Telematics penetration hit 52% in auto, enabling 8-10% premium adjustments for safe drivers, while drone inspections cut property severity leakage by 11%. We've also deployed predictive modeling from EagleView for roof claims, reducing overpayments by 14%.

Strategically, these trends affirm our portfolio optimization playbook: we've taken 9.2% rate across the book—11% in auto PD, 7% in homeowners—while non-renewing 8% of underperforming commercial risks, shrinking attritional losses by 150 bps. Reinsurance renewal in January locked in stable terms at 95% quota share on our $2.5 billion cat tower, with Swiss Re and Munich Re partners, preserving capacity headroom. Looking forward, we guide to a full-year ex-cat loss ratio of 59-60%, trending toward 57% in 2025 as severity moderates with Fed rate cuts curbing repair inflation and our tech stack matures. This positions us for mid-teens ROEs, outpacing peers like Allstate and Chubb in a normalizing market.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to dive into our new business production volume, which remains a key leading indicator of our top-line growth trajectory and our ability to capture market share in a dynamically evolving insurance landscape. For the quarter, we delivered $2.8 billion in annualized premium equivalent across all lines, representing a robust 18% year-over-year increase and a 12% sequential quarter-over-quarter uplift. In terms of policy count, we wrote approximately 1.2 million new policies, up 22% YoY, reflecting not just higher volumes but also a favorable shift toward higher-premium, higher-margin products.

Let me break this down by our core segments, starting with Property & Casualty, which accounted for 65% of total APE at $1.82 billion, up 25% YoY. Personal lines drove the lion's share here, with auto new business APE surging 32% to $950 million on the back of sustained rate adequacy—our average personal auto premium rose 9.2% amid ongoing supply chain pressures on repair costs and a hardening market post the 2023 catastrophe season. We issued 850,000 new auto policies, benefiting from our telematics-enabled 'DriveSafe' program, which now covers 40% of new auto submissions and has improved risk selection by reducing expected claims frequency by 15% through real-time behavioral data. Homeowners' new business grew 14% to $420 million APE, fueled by our bundled offerings and partnerships with real estate platforms like Zillow and Redfin, where embedded insurance uptake hit 28% of eligible transactions.

Commercial P&C was equally strong at $450 million APE, a 20% YoY increase and 45,000 new policies, with standout performance in small business owners' policies and cyber liability—up 35%—as clients navigate rising ransomware threats. Our AI-powered underwriting engine, underwritten in collaboration with an insurtech like Shift Technology, processed 75% of small commercial quotes in under 60 seconds, boosting conversion rates by 18% versus manual processes.

Shifting to Life & Health, which contributed $720 million APE or 26% of the total, up 8% YoY but accelerating from Q1's 5% growth. Term life new business hit $380 million APE with 280,000 policies, supported by our simplified issue platform that leverages wearable data from partners like Apple Health for accelerated underwriting—reducing time-to-issue to under 48 hours for 60% of cases. Group health volumes grew 12% to $220 million APE, driven by mid-market employer wins amid ACA exchange stabilization.

Group & Specialty rounded out at $260 million APE, up 15% YoY, with warranty and travel products gaining traction post-pandemic travel rebound.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, delivering $2.1 billion APE or 75% of total, up 21% YoY, where we've gained 1.2 points of personal auto market share per AM Best data, outpacing peers like Progressive and GEICO through aggressive digital acquisition. EMEA contributed $450 million, flat YoY but with strong underlying momentum in the UK motor market following our acquisition of a bolt-on portfolio from Aviva, adding 50,000 policies. Asia-Pacific was the growth engine at $250 million APE, surging 45% YoY on 120,000 new policies, led by our greenfield expansion in India via a bancassurance tie-up with HDFC Bank—capturing 15% YoY growth in term life amid rising middle-class affluence—and Indonesia's microinsurance push through Grab's embedded ecosystem.

Key trends underpinning this performance include a broadening rate cycle across P&C lines, with industry-wide commercial rate increases averaging 7-9% per Verisk analytics, allowing us to maintain disciplined pricing while growing volume. Our product mix shifted favorably, with high-margin universal life and cyber products now comprising 22% of new APE versus 18% last year. Digitally originated business hit a record 68% of new policies, up from 55% YoY, thanks to our revamped myApex app and chatbot integrations powered by generative AI, which have lifted lead conversion by 24%.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on three pillars: embedded insurance scale-up, targeting $500 million incremental APE by year-end through 50+ API partnerships akin to our Allstate | Square model; data-driven personalization, where predictive analytics from our Eagle Eye platform are pricing 30% more accurately for volatile risks like flood; and emerging risk innovation, with launches like parametric climate products in Florida and California to preempt cat-driven capacity flight.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 new business APE growth of 15-18% YoY, supported by seasonal tailwinds in life renewals and P&C rate momentum, though mindful of potential headwinds from softening auto frequency if mileage data trends lower. Our value of new business margin expanded 220 basis points to 28%, underscoring profitable growth.

Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Before I dive into our forward-looking guidance, let me quickly frame the combined ratio for those on the call. As you know, our combined ratio—calculated as the sum of our loss ratio and expense ratio divided into earned premiums—is the gold standard metric for underwriting profitability in property and casualty insurance. A ratio below 100% indicates an underwriting profit, and we've consistently delivered here at Apex through disciplined pricing, superior risk selection, and operational efficiencies.

Looking back at Q3, we reported a combined ratio of 97.2%, which included 4.5 points of catastrophe losses primarily from Hurricane Helene's impacts in the Southeast U.S. Excluding cats, it was a pristine 92.7%, reflecting the strength of our book. For the full year 2024, we're on track for a combined ratio of 96.5%, benefiting from mid-single-digit earned premium growth across our core lines—personal auto, homeowners, and commercial multi-peril—amid favorable rate environment.

Now, turning to guidance. For Q4 2024, we are guiding to a combined ratio of 94% to 96%. This assumes normalized catastrophe activity—around 2 to 3 points, in line with longer-term averages from RMS modeling—and continued momentum in our loss ratio improvement. Personal lines should see a 91% loss ratio, down from 93% this quarter, driven by auto frequency stabilization post the 2023-2024 repair inflation spike, where body shop costs rose 12% YoY per CCC Intelligent Solutions data. Homeowners will hold steady at 88%, with enhanced wind mitigation credits in Florida offsetting elevated large loss activity.

Expense ratio guidance remains anchored at 32.5% to 33%, as we lap some COVID-era variable cost savings but offset them with our GenAI underwriting platform rollout, which has already reduced manual triage by 25% in commercial lines. This initiative, powered by partnerships like those with Guidewire and Verisk's AI-driven peril models, is yielding a 15% uplift in quote-to-bind velocity.

For the full year 2025, our combined ratio guidance is 94% to 95%, positioning us at the lower end of the industry peer set—think ahead of Travelers' 96% target but in line with Chubb's sub-95% discipline. This reflects several key drivers:

1. Pricing and Portfolio Optimization 2-3 points of improvement: We've locked in 6-8% rate adequacy across the book, with commercial property renewals at +9% amid hardening reinsurance markets. We're actively non-renewing 5% of our Florida homeowners exposure—trimming from $2.5B to $2.4B in premiums—to below 10% of total, reducing our state concentration risk post-Ian and Idalia. In Europe, our motor book benefits from 7% rate hikes in the UK and Germany, countering social inflation trends where jury awards have climbed 15% per PwC's latest claims benchmarking.

2. Loss Ratio Trends and Technical Initiatives 1-2 points: Auto severity pressures are easing—down 2% QoQ—as supply chain bottlenecks for OEM parts resolve, per IHS Markit forecasts. We've expanded telematics penetration to 45% of our personal auto policies, mirroring Progressive's Snapshot success, which has improved risk segmentation and delivered a 4-point loss ratio edge on monitored vs. standard risks. In commercial, our climate-resilient underwriting via EagleView's aerial imagery and RMS HWind has cut modeled hurricane losses by 18% on new business. Large loss frequency in liability lines remains monitored, but our excess-of-loss reinsurance tower—capped at 85% quota share with partners like Swiss Re—provides robust protection above $100M events.

3. Regional Commentary:
   - U.S. 75% of premiums: Expect 93.5% combined, with California wildfire exposure managed via 20% rate increases and parametric triggers. Southeast cats normalized post-Helene.
   - Europe 15%: 95%, buoyed by favorable weather and IFRS 17 tailwinds on reserve releases.
   - Asia-Pacific 10%: 96.5%, navigating Thailand floods but gaining from 12% premium growth in workers' comp via our Singapore hub.

Strategic Insights: This guidance embeds our "Resilient Growth" framework—shifting 10% of capital from legacy auto to high-margin specialty lines like cyber and D&O, where we project 92% combined ratios. Digital transformation, including our Apex Claims AI chatbot, targets a 2-point expense leverage by YE25, similar to Lemonade's automation playbook but scaled for our $15B book. Reinsurance costs are flat YoY at 18% of ceded premiums, thanks to retrocession efficiencies.

Risks to this guidance include above-normal cats e.g., La Niña-fueled Atlantic activity per NOAA, persistent medical inflation up 5.5% per Milliman, or regulatory headwinds like Prop 103 in California. Upside could come from accelerated rate momentum or further AI gains.

We're confident this positions Apex for 8-10% ROE expansion in 2025.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call for Apex Insurance Group. Before I hand it over to our segment leaders, let me dive into our investment performance, which remains a cornerstone of our earnings stability in this volatile macro environment. Specifically, I'd like to unpack our investment income yield, which came in at 4.35% for the quarter on our $125 billion general account portfolio – that's up 25 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 85 basis points year-over-year. This not only beat our internal targets but also outperformed the industry peer average of 4.05%, as reported in the latest NAIC filings, putting us ahead of key competitors like Travelers at 4.12% and Chubb at 4.28%.

For context, our investment income yield is calculated as the annualized net investment income – including interest, dividends, and realized gains net of investment expenses and impairments – divided by the quarter-end book value of invested assets. This metric is particularly critical for us as a P&C and life insurer, where we maintain a conservative ALM framework to match our long-duration liabilities, such as annuity reserves and long-tail property-casualty claims. At 4.35%, this yield generated $1.35 billion in net investment income, representing 28% of our overall pre-tax operating income – a testament to the tailwinds from the Fed's rate-hiking cycle.

Let me break down the key drivers and trends. First, reinvestment yields were the standout, averaging 5.18% on new purchases – our highest in over a decade. With the 10-year Treasury yield hovering around 4.25% amid the inverted yield curve, we opportunistically layered in $8.2 billion of new fixed maturities at attractive levels. Our portfolio allocation remains defensively positioned: 72% investment-grade fixed income down slightly from 75% last quarter as we trimmed duration, 14% equities primarily dividend aristocrats like those in the S&P 500 Dividend ETF, 8% alternatives including core REITs and infrastructure debt, and 6% cash equivalents for liquidity buffers. Credit quality is pristine – 92% NAIC 1-rated, with an average rating of AA- per S&P – which helped us sidestep the credit migration risks that plagued some peers during last year's regional bank turmoil.

Regionally, our U.S.-centric portfolio benefited immensely, with domestic corporates yielding 5.1% on average, driven by widening investment-grade spreads to 105 basis points over Treasuries. On the technical front, we're leveraging cutting-edge initiatives to sustain and enhance these yields. Our new AI-powered portfolio optimization platform, developed in partnership with BlackRock's Aladdin suite and customized for insurance ALM, has improved our spread duration capture by 15 basis points through real-time convexity adjustments and scenario modeling under NAIC's updated Principles-Based Reserving. We've also executed a $2.5 billion liability-driven investment swap overlay to hedge interest rate volatility, locking in forward yields above 4.75% for our $40 billion annuity block. Additionally, our structured credit team deployed $1.1 billion into CLO AAA tranches at 6.2% yields, maintaining strict underlying loan diversity to mitigate idiosyncratic risks – a move that's already added 8 basis points to our earned yield run-rate.

Strategically, this positions us exceptionally well amid evolving industry dynamics. With catastrophe losses moderating post-Irma-like events and premium rates firming at +8% industry-wide per AM Best, we're derisking selectively – shortening portfolio duration from 5.8 to 5.4 years to better align with our 6.2-year liability duration – while hunting for total return alpha in a higher-for-longer rate regime. Compared to Berkshire Hathaway's more equity-heavy approach yielding 4.8% but with higher volatility, our fixed-income tilt delivers superior risk-adjusted returns, supporting our 12.5% RBC ratio.

Looking ahead, we guide to a full-year 2024 investment income yield of 4.45% to 4.55%, assuming no recessionary credit dislocations and 10-year yields stabilizing at 4.0-4.5%. Upside could come from further Fed cuts creating reinvestment opportunities in munis and ABS, while we're monitoring China real estate spillovers on our limited EM exposure. Our team remains disciplined, with a keen eye on maintaining our edge over peers like Progressive and Allstate through disciplined ALM and tech-enabled alpha generation.
